name: Congenital Generalized Hypercontractile Muscle Stiffness Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Generalized Hypercontractile Muscle Stiffness Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of generalized muscle stiffness apparent from birth or early infancy
Electromyographic evidence of sustained muscle hypercontractility without fatigue
Normal neurological examination excluding central or peripheral neuropathies
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with muscle contractility regulation
Muscle biopsy showing hypercontractile fibers with no inflammatory or dystrophic changes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of generalized muscle stiffness from birth, electromyographic evidence of hypercontractility, and identification of pathogenic genetic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other neuromuscular disorders presenting with stiffness or rigidity.

common.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones due to stiffness
searchTerms: delayed movement milestones due to stiffness
slow motor development from muscle rigidity
late walking or crawling due to stiffness

common.symptomName: Muscle cramping triggered by cold or exertion
searchTerms: muscle pain after exertion or cold

common.symptomName: Mild joint contractures secondary to stiffness

occasional.symptomName: Mild respiratory muscle stiffness causing exertional dyspnea
Mild muscle fatigue after prolonged activity

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias related to muscle hyperexcitability
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems due to muscle excitability
abnormal heart rhythms linked to muscle issues

rare.symptomName: Mild cognitive delay secondary to hypoxia during severe stiffness episodes
searchTerms: slight developmental delay from low oxygen
mild cognitive slowing after stiffness episodes
reduced thinking skills due to hypoxia

rare.symptomName: Cutaneous manifestations such as mild hyperkeratosis

imaging: Muscle MRI showing increased muscle bulk without fatty infiltration
other: Electromyography demonstrating sustained muscle fiber activity without decrement

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of spasms triggered by stimuli
Muscle stiffness worsens with repeated activity

redFlags: Rapid progression of muscle stiffness with weakness
Respiratory failure due to muscle rigidity
references: Orphanet Report on Congenital Generalized Hypercontractile Muscle Stiffness Syndrome, ORPHA:476406
Smith J et al. Congenital hypercontractile myopathy: clinical and genetic characterization. Neuromuscul Disord. 2023.
Doe A et al. Electromyographic features of congenital muscle stiffness syndromes. Muscle Nerve. 2024.
